what_its_for: Repaglinide is used to lower blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It helps your pancreas release more insulin after meals to keep your blood sugar from rising too high. It is used along with a healthy diet and exercise.
how_to_take: Take repaglinide by mouth with or without food, but it works best when taken 15 to 30 minutes before each main meal. Only take it when you are about to eat a meal. If you skip a meal, skip that dose too. Do not take it if you are not going to eat. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your blood sugar levels and other medications. The usual starting dose is 0.5 mg before each meal if you are new to diabetes medication, or 1 to 2 mg before each meal if you have taken other diabetes pills before. The maximum dose is 4 mg per meal, and no more than 16 mg per day. You may take it 2, 3, or 4 times a day depending on how many meals you eat. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and you have already skipped that meal or you are not planning to eat, do NOT take the missed dose. Simply skip it. Never double up on doses to make up for a missed one, as this can cause dangerously low blood sugar. Just take your next dose before your next meal as usual.
storage: Store repaglinide at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid skipping meals after taking repaglinide, as this can cause low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Limit or avoid alcohol, as it can cause unpredictable changes in your blood sugar. Avoid taking gemfibrozil (a cholesterol medicine) with repaglinide unless your doctor specifically approves it, as this combination can cause very low blood sugar. Be careful when driving or using heavy machinery, especially until you know how this medicine affects you, since low blood sugar can affect your alertness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience signs of low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, dizziness, confusion, rapid heartbeat, blurred vision, or fainting. Also contact your doctor if you have signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision. Call your doctor if you develop yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, unusual tiredness, or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Repaglinide starts working quickly, usually within 30 minutes of taking it, and reaches its peak effect about 1 hour after a dose. You may notice improvements in your blood sugar readings within the first few days, but it may take several weeks to see the full benefit. Keep checking your blood sugar as directed by your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and older) may be more sensitive to repaglinide and have a higher risk of low blood sugar, so they should be monitored carefully. Repaglinide is NOT recommended for use in children. If you have liver problems, your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. If you have kidney problems, your doctor will also evaluate whether dose adjustments are needed. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor before using this medicine, as insulin is usually preferred for managing blood sugar during pregnancy. It is not known if repaglinide passes into breast milk, so talk to your doctor before breastfeeding.
